title: Routine mixed traffic · RWY 23
brief: Work combined tower and approach positions. AFR123 starts at 13,000 ft with 30 NM to fly to CCB on W118 via SATBI. DLH908 enters one NM inside Coimbatore CTA B on W43 from DODSI at 12,000 ft. Without controller instructions, both arrivals follow their routes to CCB and enter its published hold. DLH908 is expected over CCB first and has the lower holding level. Issue a heading to take an aircraft out of the hold. Entry levels represent a simulated coordinated release to approach. Vector and descend both aircraft for ILS Z RWY 23. White dotted tracks show published CCB routes from the July 2026 AAI edition. Each edge label names the next fix beyond CTA B. Issue BAW452 a departure clearance: runway, turn direction, CCB outbound radial, climb flight level and squawk. Check its readback, then issue a separate explicit takeoff clearance. UAE681 enters on W43 from DODSI with 40 NM remaining to CCB, calls approach at entry (no later than 35 NM), and stays on W43 through CCB, LENBO and UGABA unless vectored. Both tower and approach are simulated. Departures request Kochi 128.300 near the outer CTA boundary; the overflight requests HAL 127.700. Earlier transfers are permitted. After transfer, aircraft stop responding but remain on radar until lateral CTA exit, continuing their last clearance. Arrival tower handoffs use 118.150. MATS Part 1 Edition 7 sections 4.11.7.5, 7.9.3 and 12.9 govern readbacks, takeoff and separate frequency changes. Receiving frequencies and combined positions are scenario assumptions.

title: Level changeover and departure clearance · RWY 23
brief: Training assumptions: combined Training Control, approach and tower. AFR123 enters W43 at FL180; clear it to FL130, then separately contact Coimbatore Approach 120.050 for its approach check-in. Issue BAW452 a complete departure clearance (runway, turn, CCB radial, climb flight level, squawk), verify its readback, then clear takeoff separately. BAW452 requests Kochi 128.300 near the outer CTA boundary, or may be transferred earlier. After external transfer it is no longer contactable but continues its last clearance until lateral CTA exit. MATS Part 1 Edition 7 sections 4.11.7.5, 7.9.3 and 12.9 apply; transfer levels and receiving arrangements are exercise assumptions.
